data.text: [00:00]CD1 Track 41
I = Interviewer, A = Alanna

[00:03.9]Welcome to Tourism Today – the programme that looks at aspects of tourism throughout the world. `[00:22.3]Today, we’re talking about a tourist destination in Europe. `[00:27]With its fantastic summer weather and beautiful islands, Greece is extremely popular with holiday makers. `[00:34]An expert on the Greek islands, Alanna Papadakis, is here to talk about some changes – both positive and negative – that are happening there. … Hello, Alanna.
[00:44.4]Hello, Mike.
[00:45]Greece is a major tourist destination. `[00:48.7]And many of the islands – like Crete, Mykonos and Santorini – are familiar to us from the tourist guides … most of us know these names.

[00:57.6]Yes, that’s right. `[00:59]Many Greek islands are well-prepared for the hordes of tourists who come every summer. `[01:04.8]These islands expect to see thousands of visitors every year. `[01:08.8]Other islands remain quiet and undiscovered by tourists though … and many of them will stay that way.
[01:16]One island, however, may soon change dramatically. `[01:20]Tell us about that …

[01:021]Well … Skopelos is an island in the Aegean Sea to the east of Athens. `[01:27]It’s very small – there are only 4,696 residents there … and yes, they might need to prepare for a huge increase in tourists.
[01:38]Four thousand six hundred and ninety-six residents – that is small! So, what’s going on there?

[01:044.8]There are reports that some tourists want to get married there. `[01:49]Others want to have parties in their own private bay. `[01:52]Others just want to dance on the beach. It’s called the Mamma Mia! effect – and it seems everyone wants to go to Skopelos now. `[02:01.6]It all started when the film Mamma Mia! was released. `[02:05.5]You know … the film version of the musical … the hit Abba musical, starring Meryl Streep, Colin Firth and Pierce Brosnan.
[02:13.3]It’s proving to be hugely popular, isn’t it?

[02:16.3]Yes, not only the film … but also the island! `[02:20]Until they started filming Mamma Mia!, Skopelos was famous for plums, pears and pine forests. `[02:27]It was a surprise to everyone that the island itself became one of the biggest stars of the film!
[02:33]Why did they choose this particular island?

[02:36.6]Well, producers looked at about twenty-five Greek islands before they decided on Skopelos. `[02:43]In the end, they chose this one because it has many different places which fitted with the story.
[02:48.9]Can you tell us exactly where some of those places are?

[02:51.9]Yes … some of the film takes place around Kastani Bay and the beaches there. `[02:58]Other parts were filmed at the top of the cliffs, above Glisteri Beach. `[03:03]That’s where the main character – played by Meryl Streep – has a house.
[03:08.4]And what about the famous wedding scene at the end of the film?
[03:11.8]Yes, the wedding scene is filmed on the mountain on the peninsula near Glisteri. It’s beautiful … unforgettable really.

[03:20.6]So, this beautiful location provided the backdrop for an extremely successful film. `[03:26.4]But will the film bring success for the island of Skopelos? Or will the changes have a negative effect?

[03:33.8]Well, things will change there. `[03:37]Sometimes films like this have a huge effect on the location. `[03:41.9]Skopelos won’t stay the same – it won’t be the same unknown place that it used to be. `[03:47.7]There’s a positive side and a negative side, I suppose. … On the negative side, things may be less peaceful. `[03:55.5]The local people may not keep the peaceful atmosphere of the island completely. `[04:00.7]But on the positive side, they are pleased to get more business, at least during the summer months.
[04:06.9]Yes, the film might be very good for business …
[04:09.5]Mmm … and I’m sure the Mamma Mia! effect will increase tourism on other islands.
[04:14.6]Yes, it might increase tourism for the whole of Greece, but … at the moment, nobody really knows if these changes will be positive or not … in the long run, I mean …
